title: Oliver at his peak and the slow march tempo of High Society
summary: Oliver's playing polished up from the rough Big 25 days. High Society was originally a slow, dirge-like supper march, not a dance tune. Russell says Black dances used Gettysburg and the 6-8 in the same way.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: That's one they clipped out for me on Golden Crest. And, well, even, I'm trying to think of some of the others that they used to sing. They were all foul. But anyway, many times, our group of six and seven-eighths wouldn't dance at all. Most of us would just hang around the band and watch and listen. We never did come anywhere near to what they were doing, but at least we'd learn the tunes and try to do it a little bit the way they did. And I remember Oliver impressing me even more up there because I think, to me, that was when he was at his peak. But he had to change his style a little bit from what I'd heard him playing down at Big 25, somewhere in the interim there. And that was rough stuff. And they began polishing it up when they went to the gym to adapt themselves to the dancers. They couldn't dance to the kind of music, although they liked the sound of it, and they realized it. And I come back to this point that I made several times. I think I've referred to it in an article that they accidentally, upon purpose, they clipped out, was the fact that high society was used not as a dance tune when they'd say, when you'd have a party and it was for a plate lunch or supper around 11.30. They'd get the couples together by playing a march. And it was an interminable march. They'd play that intro. That went on and on. And so slow, it was like a dirge march almost. Nobody could dance to high society. Then when the people began insisting on it being played, they stepped the tempo up. But that is not the original way they played it. They played a very slow tempo.
You know, some of the colored dances they'd used is Gettysburg, the 6-8 to start with, sort of the pistachio. Yes, that's exactly it.
